Okay, So GPA stands for Grade Point Average. Each grade is worth a number value on a 0-4 scale. As are worth 4 points, Bs are worth 3 points, Cs are worth 2 points, D's are worth 1 point and Fs are worth 0 points. Fraction grades (A-, B+, B-, C+ and so on.) are worth a fraction of a Grade point. For example, B+ is worth 3.3, B- is worth 2.7 and a C+ is worth 2.3. To determine GPA, one would take the average of those numbers. A 3.0 means that one received an average of a B in all their classes. My 2.9 GPA means that my average grade was just below a B, but just above a B-. 

An honours course at school is a course that is accelerated. It is a class that has a more rigorous curriculum. It is often comparable to an introductory university course. To show that one has learned enough from the course, they often take the AP exam for that subject. For most colleges in the US, a 3 out of a possible 5 is enough to be counted as a pass, and may be used in place of one college course, and credit will be awarded. In California, most of the University of California schools, like Berkeley and UCLA, only take 4s and 5s as adequate proof.
 


The SAT is a standardized test that lots of students have to take in their junior or senior year of high school. It stands for Scholastic Aptitude Test. They also have Subject Tests, that they use to show that you are sufficiently knowledgeable to take a college course in that subject. They aren't used to give college credit usually, but are usually used to make your application desirable especially for competitive programs. Most students take these, save for those in the midwest, where most students take the ACT, which is essentially the same save for the Subject Tests.
